items.description: The boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of the SQLAlchemy session or any database connection object
The service module (app/services/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy or ORM symbol
The boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of any ORM model class from app/models/
The application reads the database connection string exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable; no hardcoded connection string is present in application source code
Rendering <App> in MemoryRouter at route /stock/file mounts the stock filing form with its required input data-testid seams (sku, location, quantity, inventory_code)
POSTing a stock filing with a uuid-suffixed SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code returns a success response and the record is subsequently retrievable via the API
Submitting the stock filing form at route /stock/file with a mocked successful API response transitions the form to a visible success state
POSTing a stock filing with a missing required field returns an error response whose body names the offending field
When the stock service is called with a negative quantity value, it raises a validation error before any database statement is executed
The integration test suite connects via DATABASE_URL to the real paired branch database with Alembic migrations applied and instantiates no in-memory or mocked database driver
An insert to stock_records that omits any of sku, location, quantity, or inventory_code is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint on the real branch database
A direct database-level insert to stock_records with quantity less than zero is rejected by the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint on the real branch database

The Alembic downgrade for the stock_records migration removes the table from the real branch database and the subsequent single-step upgrade recreates it without error (@pytest.mark.migration; downgrade to base is not used)

After the stock_records migration upgrade is applied to the real branch database, rows seeded with a per-run-unique (sku, location) key are retrieved with quantity, sku, location, inventory_code, created_at, and updated_at each matching the inserted values
Every request handler in app/routes/ returns a JSON response; no handler invokes server-side template rendering
GETting a stock record that was previously filed via POST returns the exact quantity that was submitted
GETting a stock record that was previously filed via POST returns the exact combined inventory_code that was submitted
Rendering <App> in MemoryRouter at the stock record display route mounts the stock record display component with its required data-testid seams
The stock record display renders the quantity value exactly as returned by the mocked API response
The stock record display renders the inventory_code value exactly as returned by the mocked API response
POSTing a second stock filing for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair returns a success response with no error
After a second stock filing for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair, the API returns exactly one record for that pair
Filing stock for an existing SKU and location pair, when the API returns an updated record, does not display an error element in the form
Filing stock for an existing SKU and location pair, when the API returns an updated record, shows the updated values in the form
Filing stock for the same per-run-unique (sku, location) pair twice produces exactly one row in stock_records scoped to that test pair
The row surviving a (sku, location) collision upsert carries the quantity and inventory_code values submitted in the second file call
Filing stock for a (sku, location) pair that already exists leaves the existing row's created_at timestamp unchanged after the in-place upsert
Two concurrent upsert calls targeting the same per-run-unique (sku, location) key produce exactly one row in stock_records for that pair with no duplicate stored
